back: The movement of cash into (inflows) and out of (outflows) a business over a period.
Profit is counted when a sale is made; cash only when money moves. Credit sales and purchases, buying assets, inventory and loans make them differ.
Unable to pay debts when they are due; creditors may take action and the business may close even if it is profitable.
To pay suppliers, wages, bills and loan repayments, and to take opportunities such as cash discounts.
Long credit to customers, bad debts, overtrading, too much inventory, large asset purchases, poor forecasting, seasonal demand.
Overdraft; delay payments to suppliers; ask customers to pay sooner; delay buying non-current assets; lease; sell surplus stock.
Expanding faster than the cash available, so cash runs out before extra sales bring money in.
Closing balance = opening balance + (total inflows − total outflows).
A short gap suits an overdraft or delayed payment; a long-term problem needs higher sales, lower costs or long-term finance.
